company.name: Parla
company.description: Language learning app built around ten-minute speaking sessions, with a free tier and a paid subscription.

title: Parla: growth at any cost?
brief: Parla has two million installs and a retention problem. The board wants growth, the CEO has seen what competitors launched, and partnerships has three companies asking for custom versions. Buried in the backlog are a few tickets that look like housekeeping and are not. Plan the sprint, and be ready to replan it.

hidden.keyInsight: Of the 39 tickets, 12 are traps and 3 critical problems are filed as minor. The best sprint delivers 1303 points of value with 20 tickets, using 57 of 57 story points.
hidden.principle: Tech debt is paid in capacity, and risk is paid all at once. Know which dull tickets buy time and which prevent a disaster.

stakeholders.name: Kofi
priorities: Hit the growth number promised to the board
Have something impressive to show investors

stakeholders.name: Leila
priorities: Sign the corporate partners in the pipeline
Give partners what they ask for

stakeholders.name: Jonas
priorities: Fix what customers complain about every day

stakeholders.name: Ingrid
priorities: Time to pay down tech debt

stakeholders.name: Andrés
priorities: More signups from the same traffic
A launch to talk about every month

tickets.title: Social feed so users can follow each other
tickets.description: Community is our moat. Users should be able to follow friends, like their activity and comment.

visible.impactHint: Community is our moat.

hidden.explanation: A slogan instead of evidence. Nobody has checked whether users know anyone else on the app, and a feed brings moderation costs forever.

tickets.title: Smartwatch app
tickets.description: Lots of our users must own a smartwatch. A companion app would keep us on their wrist.

visible.impactHint: Lots of our users must own one.

hidden.explanation: 'Must own' is a guess. Device data from analytics would settle it in an hour, before an 8-point build.

tickets.title: Replace 'Something went wrong' with actionable errors
tickets.description: Every failure shows the same generic message. Users cannot tell whether to retry, fix their input or contact us.

hidden.explanation: Reduces confusion and some tickets, but it spreads thin across many small cases.

tickets.title: Main menu covers the content on small phones
tickets.description: On screens narrower than 360px the menu stays open over the page. Users have to rotate the phone to reach the primary button.

hidden.explanation: Blocks a core action for a meaningful share of mobile users, and it is quick to fix.

tickets.title: Native tablet app
tickets.description: I am sure a lot of our users would love us on a tablet. A founder friend with a similar product says tablets are huge for them.

visible.impactHint: A founder friend says tablets are huge for them.

hidden.explanation: A hunch and one anecdote. Nobody has checked how much traffic comes from tablets; that check takes an afternoon and comes before a 13-point build.

tickets.title: Fix the flaky test suite
tickets.description: One in three CI runs fails for no reason and is simply re-run. Engineers estimate half a day lost per person every week.

visible.impactHint: Roughly 10% of engineering time is lost to re-runs.

hidden.explanation: It moves no product metric, yet it hands back capacity in every future sprint. It pays for itself within two.

tickets.title: Replace blank screens with helpful empty states
tickets.description: Seven screens show nothing at all until the user creates data. Each should explain what goes there and offer the next step.

hidden.explanation: Useful polish for first-time users, with a modest effect on its own.

tickets.title: Card update form fails silently on expired cards
tickets.description: When a customer replaces an expired card, the form closes without saving and shows no error. The next renewal fails and the account is suspended.

visible.impactHint: Failed renewals are up 40% this quarter.

hidden.explanation: Customers who want to keep paying are being churned by a bug. Very high return for a small fix.

tickets.title: Help links in the app point to deleted articles
tickets.description: After the help centre migration, eleven in-app links lead to a 404 page.

hidden.explanation: Small value, but almost free. A good filler when one point is left.

tickets.title: Rewrite the pricing page before the price change
tickets.description: New prices go live on the 1st. The current page still describes the old plans and would show wrong numbers at checkout.

visible.impactHint: The new prices go live either way.

hidden.explanation: Not every CEO request is a trap. This one has a fixed date and a concrete cost if it slips: customers shown the wrong price.

tickets.title: Exclusive content pack for Solstice Hotels
tickets.description: Solstice Hotels asks for a set of content made to its guidelines and visible only to people who join through its link.

visible.impactHint: Solstice Hotels would promote us to its members.

hidden.explanation: Custom content gated for one partner, paid for with a promise of promotion. No commitment, no reuse.

tickets.title: App crashes on launch on older Android versions
tickets.description: Since the last update the app closes immediately on Android 11 and below. Users cannot get past the splash screen.

visible.impactHint: 9% of Android users are on those versions.

hidden.explanation: A whole segment of paying users is locked out. Close to critical, and not expensive.

tickets.title: AI assistant on the home screen
tickets.description: Every competitor announced an AI feature this quarter. We need a chat assistant on the home screen before the conference so there is something to demo.

visible.impactHint: The board asked what our AI story is.

hidden.explanation: Built for a demo, not for a user problem. No use case, no success metric, and a lot of cost and debt.

tickets.title: Password reset emails arrive more than 10 minutes late
tickets.description: Reset emails sit in a low-priority queue behind marketing sends. Users request the email several times, then write to support or give up.

hidden.explanation: A cheap fix for one of the top support drivers. Users who cannot log in do not complain for long: they leave.

tickets.title: Let users choose which emails they receive
tickets.description: Today it is all or nothing. Users who find one notification noisy unsubscribe from everything, including the emails that bring them back.

hidden.explanation: Protects the re-engagement channel, but the effect is indirect and gradual. Worth doing when there is room.

tickets.title: Cut cold start from 4.8 seconds to under 2
tickets.description: The app loads all content before showing the first screen. On mid-range phones users look at a logo for five seconds.

visible.impactHint: Each extra second of startup costs about 3% of sessions.

hidden.explanation: Every session of every user starts here, and the cost of slowness is measured.

tickets.title: Shorten onboarding from eleven screens to five
tickets.description: New users answer eleven questions before seeing the product. The drop is steepest on screens six to eight, which ask for things we never use.

visible.impactHint: Only 46% of installs finish onboarding.

hidden.explanation: More than half of installs never reach the product. Removing unused questions is cheap and hits the top of the funnel.

tickets.title: Upgrade the web framework two major versions
tickets.description: The current version leaves security support in nine months. The upgrade touches every page and needs a full regression pass.

visible.impactHint: Security support ends in 9 months.

hidden.explanation: Necessary, not urgent: there are nine months of runway and it would eat most of a sprint. Plan it, do not squeeze it in.

tickets.title: Private group space for Greyfield Energy's staff benefits programme
tickets.description: Greyfield Energy wants a closed area where only its staff can see each other's activity, with admin reports for its HR team.

visible.impactHint: Greyfield Energy wants to launch in a month.

hidden.explanation: A B2B feature set bolted onto a consumer app for one deal. It serves none of the subscribers who pay today.

tickets.title: A few users charged before the free trial ended
tickets.description: Six tickets this month say 'I was charged on day 5 of a 7-day trial'. Support refunded them. Maybe a time zone issue.

hidden.explanation: Charging before the promised date is a billing violation. Six people wrote in; many more were charged and went to their bank or the store instead.

tickets.title: Move content to a CMS
tickets.description: Changing a sentence in the app requires a release and a store review. The content team waits a week for typo fixes.

visible.impactHint: Copy changes take a week to reach users.

hidden.explanation: Unblocks the content team and reduces releases. Worth doing, without urgency.

tickets.title: Search: typo tolerance and recent items
tickets.description: Search only matches exact words. One in five queries returns nothing, and most of those are misspellings of things that exist.

visible.impactHint: 21% of searches return zero results.

hidden.explanation: A real, measured friction for regular users. Solid mid-value work, though not cheap.

tickets.title: Weekly summary email
tickets.description: A short email every Monday with what happened in the account and one suggested action.

visible.impactHint: Our re-engagement emails get a 31% open rate.

hidden.explanation: A reasonable retention lever built on a channel that already works.

tickets.title: Apply the new brand colours across the whole app
tickets.description: The rebrand launched on the website last month. The app still uses the old palette on about 60 screens.

visible.impactHint: Users see two different brands.

hidden.explanation: Everyone sees it and nobody behaves differently because of it. It can ride along with other UI work over time.

tickets.title: Nightly backup job finishes with warnings
tickets.description: The backup job has logged warnings for three weeks. Nobody has tested a restore since the storage migration.

hidden.explanation: Three weeks of unverified backups means one bad deploy away from permanent data loss. It looks like housekeeping and is not.

tickets.title: Alerting on error rates and queue depth
tickets.description: Today the team learns about incidents from customer emails. Basic alerts would cut detection time from hours to minutes.

visible.impactHint: Last incident went unnoticed for 3 hours.

hidden.explanation: Every future incident gets shorter. High leverage for a few points.

tickets.title: Cut deploy time from 50 minutes to 10
tickets.description: A deploy blocks the pipeline for almost an hour, so fixes are batched and hotfixes are slow.

visible.impactHint: The team deploys twice a week instead of daily.

hidden.explanation: Speeds up every release and every hotfix. Good value, but not a small job.

tickets.title: Scheduled items fire at the wrong hour outside UTC
tickets.description: Anything scheduled is stored without a time zone. Users in other zones get reminders and reports hours early or late.

hidden.explanation: A correctness bug in a feature people rely on, affecting everyone outside one time zone. Cheap to fix.

tickets.title: Ask for notification permission after the first goal is set
tickets.description: The system permission prompt appears on the first screen, with no explanation. Most people tap 'Don't allow' and can never be reminded.

visible.impactHint: Opt-in rate is 31%; comparable apps reach 50%.

hidden.explanation: Notifications are the main way back into the app. Moving one prompt recovers a channel lost for most users.

tickets.title: Co-branded version of the app for Castellan Foods
tickets.description: Castellan Foods wants to offer the app to its employees with its own logo, colours and a custom welcome flow.

visible.impactHint: Castellan Foods has 8,000 employees.

hidden.explanation: A second app to maintain for one partner. Headcount is not usage: a discount code gives them the same benefit with no build.

tickets.title: Navigation is unusable on narrow screens
tickets.description: On the smallest phones the open menu sits on top of the page and hides the main button. Found during the last design review.

hidden.explanation: Same work as PRL-280 ("Main menu covers the content on small phones"), described by a different team. Shipping both delivers the value once and pays for the effort twice.

tickets.title: Signup accepts birth years that make users under 13
tickets.description: Analytics shows about 2% of new accounts enter a birth year after 2013. We do not do anything with the field.

hidden.explanation: Knowingly collecting data from children without parental consent breaks child privacy law. The penalty is fines and removal from the stores.

tickets.title: Offer an annual plan at checkout
tickets.description: Only the monthly plan is sold. An annual option at a discount would lock in the users most likely to stay.

visible.impactHint: Monthly subscribers churn at 9% a month.

hidden.explanation: With 9% monthly churn, an annual plan changes the economics of every subscriber who takes it. Small build.

tickets.title: Android sessions ending within two seconds of launch
tickets.description: Dashboards show a block of Android sessions that end almost as soon as they start, all from older devices. Something fails at startup for them.

hidden.explanation: Same work as PRL-301 ("App crashes on launch on older Android versions"), described by a different team. Shipping both delivers the value once and pays for the effort twice.

tickets.title: 3D avatars users can dress up
tickets.description: Let every user create an avatar and unlock outfits. Younger users love this kind of thing.

visible.impactHint: Younger users love this kind of thing.

hidden.explanation: A generalisation about an age group, not a need of our users. Enormous build with no link to why people subscribe.

tickets.title: App store requirement: update the SDK by the 28th or be removed from sale
tickets.description: The store sent a final notice. Apps built with the old SDK are removed from search and cannot be updated after the 28th.

visible.impactHint: Final notice: the 28th.

hidden.explanation: After the date there are no new installs and no way to ship fixes. An external deadline that ends the business if missed.

tickets.title: We find out about outages from customers
tickets.description: Support learns that something is down when tickets pile up, then tells engineering. The system should warn engineering first.

visible.impactHint: Three incidents this quarter were reported by customers.

hidden.explanation: Same work as PRL-330 ("Alerting on error rates and queue depth"), described by a different team. Shipping both delivers the value once and pays for the effort twice.

tickets.title: Let users choose their reminder time
tickets.description: Reminders go out at 9:00 for everyone. People who are busy at that hour mute them within days.

visible.impactHint: 40% of users mute reminders within a week.

hidden.explanation: A reminder at the wrong time is noise. A small setting keeps the main retention channel alive.

tickets.title: 'Restore purchases' fails after reinstalling
tickets.description: Subscribers who change phone or reinstall are asked to pay again. Restore does nothing for accounts created with email.

hidden.explanation: Paying customers are denied what they bought. Each case is a refund, a bad review or both.

midSprintEvents.title: Tomás is out for the rest of the sprint
midSprintEvents.description: Tomás, one of the senior engineers, is on unexpected leave from today. Their work in progress has to be picked up by the rest of the team.

hidden.guidance: Capacity dropped, so scope has to drop with it. Cut the lowest-value work and protect the critical tickets. Asking the team to absorb the difference is how sprints fail quietly.

midSprintEvents.title: Leila promised Pinnacle Freight a custom data feed by the end of the sprint
midSprintEvents.description: On a call yesterday Leila told Pinnacle Freight they would have a nightly data feed in their own format before the sprint ends. The contract is not signed yet. Leila says the deal depends on it.

addedTicket.title: Nightly data feed in Pinnacle Freight's format
addedTicket.description: Build a nightly export to Pinnacle Freight's file server, in the column layout and naming they specified.

visible.impactHint: Promised to Pinnacle Freight for the end of this sprint.

hidden.explanation: A bespoke feed for an account that has not signed. The promise was made without the team, and a standard export covers what they need.

hidden.guidance: A promise made without the team is the start of a negotiation, not a commitment. Find out what the customer actually needs and offer the standard option or a later date. Do not trade work that helps everyone for one unsigned deal.
